papers.title: Second Moments of Hecke Traces and Vertical Sato–Tate
papers.abstract: We relate sums of squared Hecke traces to the distribution of Frobenius traces of elliptic curves over $\mathbf{F}_p$. For every fixed $1/6\le a<1/2$, the sum of squared normalized traces at level one up to weight $K=p^a$ is asymptotic to $K^2/48$ on a density-one set of primes. In the same range, fixed-level limits hold on sets of relative density one in the relevant prime classes, with constants that factor over prime powers. We compute the mixed moments between newform spaces at different levels and between character spaces at odd prime level. The connection comes from tossing a coin whose bias is determined by the trace of a uniformly chosen nonsingular Weierstrass equation. The Sato–Tate predictor's excess log loss tends to zero exactly when $T=o(p)$. For $T=\lfloor\lambda K^2\rfloor$ with fixed $\lambda>0$ it is asymptotic to $T/(96p)$ on the level-one prime set. When $T/p\to c>0$, we compute the limiting losses along prime subsequences whose residues stabilize modulo each fixed integer. The two nonzero classes modulo $3$ can give different limits. At level one we compute the leading variances across prime intervals for the normalized trace sum and the normalized chi-square divergence.

papers.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
papers.abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

papers.title: Sharp inequalities and stability for real profiles on arithmetic progressions
papers.abstract: Real bounded observables obey extremal laws that differ from those of complex polynomial phases. We prove that a centred real observable on a totally ergodic system satisfies $\|F\|_{U^3}^{8}\leq 1/3$. Equality holds precisely for signs of semicircles on a Kronecker circle factor, and near equality forces proximity in $L^1$ to this class, uniformly over all systems. For four such signs at consecutive times we classify the maximising frequencies and phases, and obtain a gap to $1/4$ when no relation with coefficients in $\{-1,1\}$ is present. We then determine the exact range of four-term averages with prescribed horizontal projections and realise every value in one totally ergodic extension with an enlarged Kronecker factor. For seven real profiles on a common quadratic Haar progression, we determine both the lower convex boundary at two fixed anchor means and the boundary attainable by a single tuple when those means vanish. Their separation has optimal coefficient $(4-\sqrt2)/3$. Finally, an explicit continuous family of four-profile configurations retains correlation $1/3$ while its interior profiles cease to be semicircle signs. The proofs combine connected-group rearrangement, an autocorrelation tail inequality, compactness of ordered Fourier coefficients, and exact finite lattice checks.

papers.title: Sharp linear bounds for the EKG sequence
papers.abstract: We prove that the EKG sequence satisfies $13n/28\le a(n)\le12n/7$ for every $n\ge1$, with equality only at $n=28$ and $n=7$, respectively. Discovered by Jonathan Ayres, the sequence starts with $1,2$ and repeatedly takes the least unused positive integer sharing a factor greater than $1$ with its predecessor. This proves the sharp linear bounds conjectured by Lagarias, Rains and Sloane, who established coarse bounds at every index. Hofman and Pilipczuk proved the limits $1/2$, $3/2$ and $1$ of $a(n)/n$ on primes, their triples and the other terms, and Haver made these estimates explicit and formalized them in Lean. Our earlier second-order asymptotic also builds on Haver's work. We sharpen Haver's self-improving early-even bound with a shorter prime window and effective large-sieve constants, and control odd terms so that the analytic range meets a finite computation. Lean checks the deduction from the definition, conditional on computed premises; independent programs check those premises, and their correspondence with the formal statements was checked by reading the code. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization, the programs and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: Sign changes of Kloosterman sums on moduli with at most three prime factors
papers.abstract: For each sign, we prove that \(\gg X/\log X\) squarefree moduli in \((X,2X]\) with at most three prime factors have a normalized Kloosterman sum of that sign with magnitude bounded below by a positive constant. The bound extends to short arithmetic progressions, uniformly for nonzero coefficients in a small power range. The proof combines Sato--Tate marginals for complementary blocks of prime factors with a centered linear divisor weight.

papers.title: Simultaneous quadratic probes: reconstruction thresholds and marked Poisson limits
papers.abstract: We observe a uniformly chosen integer in $[X,2X)$ through the four Legendre symbols of $n,n+1,3n+1,3n+2$ at each of $k$ randomly chosen distinct primes congruent to $3$ modulo $8$. Our main arithmetic estimate compares simultaneous collision probabilities with those of independent uniform words, in absolute mean at the critical scale. It includes tuples with deficient square-class rank and permits arbitrary deterministic binary labels fixed before the primes are sampled. We deduce a threshold at $k=\log_{16}X$: below it by a diverging additive amount, optimal identification tends to zero uniformly over panels. In probability over the panel, the observation becomes independent of the label below the threshold, and the proportion of origins with a unique observation tends to one above it by a diverging additive amount. If $X/16^k\to\rho$ and the positive-label proportion tends to $\alpha$, the empirical marked occupancy law converges in probability to independent Poisson laws of means $\rho\alpha$ and $\rho(1-\alpha)$. Classical occupancy calculations then give explicit identification and prediction limits. For primes in $(Y/2,Y]$ we treat $\log\log X=o(\log Y)$, $\log Y=o(\log X)$ by the quadratic large sieve, and $Y=(\log X)^A$, for each fixed $A>2$, by a prime-character estimate under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions. The independently checked zero theorem announced by Alpöge supplies this last hypothesis. The proof combines square-class separation, the quadratic large sieve and averaged exponentiation of prime-character estimates. For the quartic Liouville label, an existing bound on ordinary averages and fixed-ratio isotopy constrain its mark density outside a set of scales of logarithmic density zero.

papers.title: Small roots of split quadratic congruences and fundamental units in a quartic family
papers.abstract: We study two questions about square classes associated with the forms $n$, $n+1$, $3n+1$ and $3n+2$. For the least positive integer $k\ne3$ for which $(kn+1)/(3n+1)$ is a rational square, we prove $\log(n^2/K_*(n))=2(\log2)\omega(n)+O(\log\log\log n)$ on a set of natural density one. The proof combines an exact second moment for dilated congruence roots with a weighted sieve that includes every rational denominator. The same estimates give $\log(n/(r_n+2))=(\log2)\omega(n)+O(\log\log\log n)$ on a density-one set for the least nonnegative root of $(r+1)(r+3)\equiv0\pmod n$. This establishes its normal-order exponent $\log2$ predicted by Crişan and Pollack for this polynomial. Both Gaussian limit laws follow from Erdős–Kac. Second, write $D(n)=n(n+1)(3n+1)(3n+2)=d_ns_n^2$ with $d_n$ squarefree. The unit $9n(n+1)+1+3s_n\sqrt{d_n}$ is fundamental in the full ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d_n})$ except for at most $\exp(O((\log X)^{2/3}))$ indices $n\le X$; there are at least a constant multiple of $\log X$ exceptions. The upper bound specializes Alpöge's integral-point descent using the splitting fields of a Chebyshev family. A final change of index retains the Liouville sign in a series over fundamental regulators. It transports local holomorphic continuation at $s=1$ equivalently between the two signed series, yielding a conditional cancellation criterion.

papers.title: Solvable points on intersections of quadrics, cubics, and quartics
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not 2 or 3. We establish polynomial bounds on the ambient dimension $N$, such that if $N$ is at least as big as this bound, every intersection $X\subset\mathbb{P}^N$ of quadrics, cubics and quartics has a solvable point, and a general one has a dense collection of solvable points, i.e. points in $X(k^{\mathrm{Sol}})$ where $k^{\mathrm{Sol}}/k$ is a solvable closure. Our method connects the classical theory of polar hypersurfaces to Fano varieties $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$ of linear subspaces on $X$, and we use this to obtain improved control on the arithmetic of $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$

papers.title: Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four
papers.abstract: A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $\eta(2z)^{4}\eta(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and level $8$. The proof reduces the counts by elementary means to a twisted second moment of the Legendre family of elliptic curves, which is a value of a hypergeometric function over $\mathbb{F}_q$ evaluated by Ahlgren and Ono for primes. As consequences, the number of factorizations whose three pairwise resultants lie in one square class is a polynomial in $q$, with proportion $1/4+3/(4q^{2})+O(q^{-4})$. When the quotient is a product of two elliptic curves conjugate over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, we prove that the splitting of the factors $u,v,w$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ decides which points of order two of the elliptic factor are divisible by two.

papers.title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente \`a la formule des traces en caract\'eristique p>0
papers.abstract: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.

papers.title: Structure theorem for cofibrant tame functors indexed by posets of dimension 1
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss certain circumstances in which the category of tame functors inherits an abelian category structure with minimal resolutions and a model category structure with minimal cofibrant replacements. We also present a structure theorem for cofibrant objects in the category of tame functors indexed by realizations of posets of dimension 1 with values in the category of chain complexes in an abelian category whose all objects are projectives. Moreover, we introduce a general technique to generate indecomposable objects in the abelian category of functors indexed by finite posets.

papers.title: Subadditivity of the smooth number counting function for every smoothness bound
papers.abstract: Let $\Psi(x,y)$ be the number of positive integers up to $x$ with no prime factor exceeding $y$. Hildebrand proved in 1985 that $\Psi(x+z,y)\le\Psi(x,y)+\Psi(z,y)$ for all $x,z\ge y$, provided that $y$ is sufficiently large, and Granville asked whether the inequality holds for all $x,z>y\ge 2$. We give an elementary proof that it does. The inequality also holds for all nonnegative integers $x$ and $z$. The proof follows Hildebrand's method, with his estimates replaced by exact statements. We are not aware of an earlier proof for all $y$, but our literature search was not exhaustive. See Section 1.2.

papers.title: Tensor semistability from rectangular Specht lattices
papers.abstract: We prove Bost's conjecture on the additivity of maximal slopes under Hermitian tensor products over the integers of any number field. For a subbundle with a geometrically semistable Pl\"ucker point, we use an invariant to detect a nonzero integral contraction between determinant components of tensor powers. The source and target are semistable by their symmetric group actions. We prove that a rectangular Specht lattice with a fixed number of rows and $a$ boxes has logarithmic covolume per rank $O(\sqrt a)$. Dividing the slope comparison by $a$ and letting $a$ tend to infinity yields the exact inequality. Weighted filtrations handle the geometrically unstable case. This argument was discovered while reconstructing Levent Alp\"oge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: The $(3,4,\infty)$ family of complex six-spheres. I. Periods, moduli and the two ends
papers.abstract: We determine the periods, moduli and two limiting regimes of the $(3,4,\infty)$ family of complex six-spheres. A theta expression for its elliptic period gives the exact parameter disc $0<|w|<216$. Integral affine and cusp comparison maps classify the discrete data, parameter identifications and real structures, including the fixed three-spheres. We compute the integral monodromy group, its maximal domain of proper discontinuity and the algebraic dimension of every smooth fibre. Logarithmic direct images and explicit relative differential modules determine the Dolbeault, Bott–Chern, Aeppli and tangent cohomology, all Picard twists and the deformation parameter. Global Dolbeault representatives extend through the multiple fibres and cusp. At the puncture, the corner monodromy obstructs every proper Hausdorff analytic filling after any finite parameter cover; the analogous obstruction holds for the coprime higher-multiplicity sphere families. At the outer boundary, the intrinsic Albanese invariant obstructs continuation, while the dual period lattices determine the local Hausdorff reflection and all additive limits. The arithmetic norm satisfies exact division and height identities; we describe its torsion values, critical points and level curves.

papers.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
papers.abstract: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

papers.title: The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua
papers.abstract: Let $(X,d)$ be a nondegenerate compact connected metric space such that, for any two distinct points $a,b\in X$, exactly two points of $X$ are equidistant from $a$ and $b$. We prove that $X$ is homeomorphic to a circle. This settles the double midset conjecture of Loveland and Wayment from 1974. It was previously known for plane continua with the Euclidean metric and under additional convexity or continuity hypotheses. No assumption on the metric is made beyond compatibility with the topology. We first show that a counterexample would be a finite tree. On a finite tree, a parity count of the sign changes of $d(\cdot,a)-d(\cdot,b)$, combined with a Baire category argument, forces whole intervals onto metric spheres. This rigidity is incompatible with a branch point and with an arc. The results of the paper are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: The Egami–Matsumoto conjecture under the Riemann Hypothesis alone: a natural boundary of the Goldbach generating series
papers.abstract: The Goldbach generating series Φ₂(s) = Σ_{m,n≥1} Λ(m)Λ(n)(m+n)^(−s) continues meromorphically to Re s > 1 under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), by a theorem of Egami and Matsumoto, who conjectured that the line Re s = 1 is its natural boundary. The complete proofs so far have assumed, besides RH, a hypothesis on additive relations among the ordinates of the zeros of ζ. We prove the conjecture under RH alone, and the corresponding statement for the series Φ_r(s) = Σ Λ(k₁)⋯Λ(k_r)(k₁+⋯+k_r)^(−s) at Re s = r − 1, for every r ≥ 2. RH can be weakened: the continuation and the boundary hold under the hypothesis H∞ that for every δ > 0 only finitely many zeros have real part greater than ½ + δ. The new step is a phase estimate for products of two Gamma values at zeros of large ordinates of opposite signs. It shows that the pairs of zeros whose sums land on one point do not cancel when every such pair consists of zeros whose ordinates exceed in modulus a threshold depending only on a bound for the imaginary part of the point; points of this kind accumulate at every point of the line, and under RH they are dense on it. Under H∞, if RH fails then Φ₂ has a simple pole with positive residue at the real point 2B ∈ (1, 2), where B is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros; so, under H∞, RH holds if and only if Φ₂ has no pole in the real interval (1, 2). A criterion of this kind, through the poles at the points 1 + ρ, follows from work of Bhowmik, Halupczok, Matsumoto and Suzuki; what is new is the pole at 2B, whose residue is a sum of positive terms. The theorems are checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant, as implications from H∞ (or RH) and classical theorems on ζ and Γ stated as hypotheses.

papers.title: The entropy photon-number inequality without an energy assumption
papers.abstract: We deduce the entropy photon-number inequality for two independent bosonic inputs of finite von Neumann entropy from OpenAI's finite-energy theorem. The result holds for any finite number of modes, even when both inputs have infinite mean photon number. Applying the same photon-number filter at both ports of the beam splitter gives an operator bound on the retained marginal and hence an upper bound on its entropy. At transmissivities strictly between zero and one, an input of infinite entropy forces the output entropy to be infinite. We also obtain the sharp minimum output entropy of a thermal attenuator at prescribed input entropy, without an energy constraint.

papers.title: The Harborth constant of Cp ⊕ Cp for every prime p ≥ 11
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the least $k$ such that every $k$-element subset of $G$ contains $\exp(G)$ distinct elements whose sum is zero; the exponent $\exp(G)$ is the largest order of an element of $G$. Gao and Thangadurai conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n-1$ for odd $n$, and proved it for primes $p\ge 67$; Gao, Geroldinger and Schmid extended this to $p\ge47$, and Kemnitz had settled $p\in\{3,5,7\}$. Bajnok's Menu of research problems asks for the primes $11\le p\le 43$ (Problem F.100). We prove that $\mathsf g(C_p\oplus C_p)=2p-1$ for every prime $p\ge11$, which answers that problem and, with Kemnitz's values, gives the conjecture for every odd prime. As in the work of Gao and Thangadurai and of Gao, Geroldinger and Schmid, we project the set along a line through $0$, which sorts its points into $p$ parallel lines (fibers), choose a projection in which many pairs of points share a fiber, and use the lifting criterion of Gao and Thangadurai. What is new is a sufficient condition, proved with the theorem of Dias da Silva and Hamidoune, that depends only on how many points each fiber holds and not on where the fibers lie. The analysis of fiber sizes is by hand for $p\ge17$ and a finite check for $p=11$ and $13$. The proof for $p\ge11$ and the lower bound for every odd prime are formalized in Lean. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: The homotopy types of $Sp(n)$-gauge groups over $S^{4m}$
papers.abstract: Let $m$ and $n$ be two positive integers such that $m < n$. Denote by $P_{n,k}$ the principal $Sp(n)$-bundle over $S^{4m}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ be the gauge group of $P_{n,k}$ classified by $k\varepsilon'$, where $\varepsilon'$ is a generator of $\pi_{4m}(B(Sp(n)))\cong\mathbb{Z}$. In this article, we will partially classify the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ by giving a lower bound for the number of homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$. Also, in special cases $Sp(3)$-gauge groups over $S^8$ and $Sp(4)$-gauge groups over $S^{12}$ we give an upper bound for the number of homotopy types of these gauge groups.

papers.title: The magic of free spheres
papers.abstract: We study integration, diffusion and vibration on the classical, half-liberated and free spheres. The latitude polynomials recover the free hyperspherical law and describe heat released at a pole outside its stationary support. On the free ball two invariant integrals admit Weingarten formulas. The divergence integral selects a radial completion on which we construct a closed energy, a completely positive Poisson extension and its boundary normal derivative. On the 2 quantum balls, degree 3 already gives nonpolynomial harmonic extensions; the free boundary spectrum has exponential multiplicities. We distinguish this radial theory from projected spherical heat and the boundary obstruction on the universal ball. Stereographic charts and mixed coordinate laws lead back to the sphere, whose wave frequencies we compare with the quantum sphere played by Connes.

papers.title: The mean square of the Goldbach error at every large endpoint
papers.abstract: For every sufficiently large $X$, the sum of squared errors in the Hardy--Littlewood prediction for the log-weighted binary Goldbach count is $\gg X^2\log^2 X$ on $(X/1000,X]$, separately in the classes $2$ and $4$ modulo six. For ordinary ordered prime pairs the lower bound is $\gg X^2/\log^2 X$. Montgomery and Vaughan obtained these orders on a sequence of sharp endpoints. We localize their norm comparison by removing the unwanted output frequencies in $L^1$. The lower bounds persist when, on each interval of a partition with interval lengths at least $X\exp(-(\log X)^{1/3})$, the singular series $\mathfrak S(k)$ in the prediction is replaced by $a\,\mathfrak S(k)+b$, with constants $a,b$ fitted from the data on that interval.

papers.title: The non symmetric Hikita conjecture
papers.abstract:
We construct local and global comparison maps for the Hikita conjecture in quiver gauge theories and study their analogues for finite non symmetric Cartan pairs. The construction uses quiver Hecke description of Coulomb branch and microlocal geometry. It yields comparison maps from B-algebras to the cohomology of some Lagrangians of quiver varieties.
  For arbitrary symmetric types, the local and global comparison maps are surjective and are isomorphisms under a B-algebra dimension bound. In finite non symmetric types, the local image is the image of the Kirwan map, i.e., the tautological subalgebra. It can be proper. Under some assumptions we also construct a non symmetric global comparison map.
  Crystal theoretic methods identify the set of nonempty Lagrangians with the set of isomorphism classes of simple modules of the category $\mathscr O$ of the Coulomb branch, and proves that the Lagrangians are nonempty for $\ell$-dominant $\ell$-highest weights.
  The proof uses microlocal modules of Coulomb branches that we define. We prove they form integral bases of the Grothendieck group of the category $\mathscr O$, with Jordan-H\"older multiplicities given by characteristic cycles.
  In symmetric type we prove an isomorphism between based quasimap modules at homogeneous polarized points of quiver varieties and co-specialized microlocal modules. The proof uses hyperbolic restriction and Braden's theorem. We conjecture an extension to all homogeneous points and a relative version.

papers.title: The Polylogarithm as a Liouville Fractional Integral and a Related Fractional Differential Equation
papers.abstract: We study the polylogarithm $\operatorname{Li}_s(z)$ from the perspective of fractional calculus. For $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(w)<0$, we express $\operatorname{Li}_s(e^{w})$ as the left Liouville fractional integral of order $s$ of the function $e^{w}/(1-e^{w})$. This gives the classical Bose–Einstein integral representation. We then consider a linear fractional differential equation with forcing term $\operatorname{Li}_s(e^{w})$. Using the eigenfunction property of exponentials under the Liouville derivative, we obtain an explicit solution in the form of a series. This series defines a parameter-dependent function $R_{\alpha,s}(z;\lambda)$, for which we establish several properties, including a reduction to a classical polylogarithm, an expansion in polylogarithms, differential relations, and its meromorphic dependence on $\lambda$.

papers.title: The queueing polynomial is convex
papers.abstract: We prove that the hypergraph polynomial arising in redundancy scheduling is convex on the nonnegative orthant for every number of vertices, every positive edge size, and every nonnegative degree. This proves Conjecture 1 of Brosch, Laurent and Steenkamp, posed in their work on job occupancy, which asks for convexity on the standard simplex for all parameters at least two. They proved convexity for edge size two and degree three; Polak's Theorem 1.1 extends the edge-size-two case through degree nine. Marshall and Olkin's classical exponential construction gives a moment representation that yields convexity directly. We apply this construction to the conjecture and give a finite proof checked in Lean. A vertex-deletion recurrence expresses the original ordered-tuple polynomial as an average of complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials at nonnegative linear forms. Their convexity follows from McLeod's classical inequality; we give a coefficientwise Hessian proof suited to formal verification. The representation and the full simplex statement are checked in Lean. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: The shapes of maximal degree 147 with starting corner (6,15) in the plane Jacobian problem
papers.abstract: In the list of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui of the possible shapes of a counterexample to the plane Jacobian conjecture with degrees at most 150, the families F7 and F8 have starting corner (6,15) and final corners (7/3,4) and (8/3,5); for degrees at most 150 they give the standard (m,n)-pairs with (m,n)=(2,7) or (7,2) (degrees 42 and 147) and (m,n)=(3,7) or (7,3) (degrees 63 and 147). We show that no such pair exists, the pair being normalised as in Corollary 5.21 of Guccione-Guccione-Valqui. The left side of the Newton polygon is controlled by a lattice argument applied to translates of the pair, after which the pair lies in an explicit polynomial ring with a weight coming from the final corner. The top part of the system has three solutions for F8, conjugate over a cubic field, and one solution for F7, over Q(sqrt(-15)). Over these fields the remaining equations are solved by linear algebra layer by layer, and the compatibility conditions, polynomials in six unknowns, generate the unit ideal; an explicit certificate 1 = sum c_i f_i is computed and checked exactly. The computation is reproduced by an ancillary script (SymPy and python-flint). All statements are proved relative to the cited results. Nothing in this note has been checked by a third party.

papers.title: The three-color Ramsey number of the 10-vertex path
papers.abstract: We prove $R(P_{10},P_{10},P_{10})=18$: every three-coloring of the edges of $K_{18}$ contains a monochromatic path on ten vertices, and some three-coloring of $K_{17}$ contains none. Faudree and Schelp suggested a formula for three-color path Ramsey numbers. Gyárfás, Ruszinkó, Sárközy and Szemerédi proved that the three-color Ramsey number of the path on $n$ vertices is $2n-2+(n\bmod2)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Dybizbański, Dzido and Radziszowski established the eight- and nine-vertex cases, completing the cases through nine vertices recorded by Radziszowski's survey. The lower-bound coloring is the even-case $K_4$ blow-up given by Gyárfás, Ruszinkó, Sárközy and Szemerédi and by Dybizbański, Dzido and Radziszowski. The new upper bound follows from Boolean satisfiability refutations after fixing a monochromatic nine-vertex path and imposing simultaneous symmetry constraints. A separate refutation proves that the cases considered cover every coloring. The reduction and the certificate checks are formalized in Lean. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization, the search code, the certificate checkers and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: The unique shortest rank-state cycle in Beggar-My-Neighbour: Six tricks and 38 individual plays
papers.abstract: Under chronological pickup and winner-led play, the minimum primitive rank-state cycle lengths for the standard 52-card inventory are six completed tricks and 38 individual plays. One cycle attains both minima and is unique under either criterion, up to cyclic phase and exchange of players. Its 30–22 witness has a short word certificate, and a 26–26 deal enters it after one trick. The trick-period proof excludes 1,201 face itineraries below six tricks and classifies all 21,407 six-trick itineraries. For the global individual-play result, an elementary bound reduces the problem to at most 18 tricks. Two independently implemented enumerators agree on all 43,808 candidate itineraries through 38 plays; exact integer gap constraints leave one itinerary and one rank-and-gap model. A short modular-arithmetic argument independently proves rigidity of that surviving model. With named players there are two oriented cycles, each with six boundary states and 181 backward-reachable rank states, including 19 balanced starts. We also classify period-four deck sizes and prove that fixed-period deck-size sets are semilinear.

papers.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $\xi$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

papers.title: There is no symmetric configuration $59_8$
papers.abstract: We prove that no symmetric configuration $59_8$ exists. The two leave graphs of a putative configuration are 2-regular. A parity-free enumeration of 29,269 cycle profiles, using integer block moments and periodicity, leaves three profiles. Cross-moment arguments exclude two mixed profiles. An anisotropic kernel form modulo 353 excludes the single-cycle case. No cyclicity or automorphism is assumed. The computation is reproducible in Python, and the unrestricted theorem has been verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Three isolated primes in the ternary Goldbach problem
papers.abstract: Every sufficiently large odd integer $N$ is the sum of three distinct primes, each at distance at least $c\log N\,(\log\log N)^{1/325565}$ from every other prime. One of the three has an isolation radius of order $\log N\,\log_2N\,\log_4N/\log_3N$. This answers the question of Maier and Rassias with the smaller growing function allowed in their remark. For all but $O(X^{1-\beta})$ even integers in $[X,2X]$, there are at least $cX^\nu$ binary representations with both primes isolated at the smaller radius, for absolute $\beta,\nu>0$. The proof keeps the centres of a two-interval covering coprime to its modulus and applies classical Goldbach theorems in arithmetic progressions.

papers.title: Total-Collapse Primes of Polynomial Maps over $\mathbb{F}_p$: Eighteen Families and Two Related Sequences
papers.abstract: For a polynomial map $T : \mathbb{F}_p \to \mathbb{F}_p$ and a nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$, a prime $p$ is a total-collapse prime for $(T, A)$ if every forward orbit in $\mathbb{F}_p$ eventually enters $A$; when $A$ is $T$-invariant and periodic, every directed cycle of $T$ on $\mathbb{F}_p$ lies in $A$. Extending Vasiga and Shallit's study of $x^2 - 2 \pmod{p}$, we study $18$ polynomial families over $\mathbb{F}_p$: seven odd cubics $\mathcal{K}_n(u) = (u^3 - (n^2 + n + 1)u)/(n(n + 1))$ (OEIS A401667), seven Chebyshev-Dickson squares $V_m(x)^2$ (OEIS A401173; drafts A399326, A402659), three Hilbert class field and octic maps (OEIS A401959, A402158; draft A399684), and $x^2(x - 2)^2$. Using dynatomic factorizations, Stickelberger's parity theorem, the dihedral group $D_7$ for $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-251})$, and Dickson's permutation criterion, we prove necessary conditions for total collapse in each family. Along the cubic ladder $\mathcal{K}_n$ (OEIS A398745), whenever $n^2 + (n + 1)^2 = c^2$ ($n \in \text{A001652}$, $c \in \text{A001653}$), total collapse for $p > n + 1$ requires $c$ prime and $p = c$. We also study sums of $n$-bit one-zero-block primes (OEIS A401666) and certify prime tables across all $20$ sequences.

papers.title: Transitive sets and Graham's radius conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonempty finite Euclidean Ramsey set of circumradius $\rho$ is Ramsey on sufficiently high-dimensional spheres of every prescribed radius $R>\rho$. We include and use an elementary proof that all finite transitive Euclidean sets are Ramsey. We also use the solvable dense block theorem derived from the Kneser--shift theorem and adapt the necessity argument from OpenAI's characterization of Ramsey sets.

papers.title: Two shapes of maximal degree 147 in the plane Jacobian problem: exclusion of the degree pairs (147,98) and (98,147) with corners (7,42) and (13/7,6)
papers.abstract: In the list of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui of the possible shapes of a counterexample to the plane Jacobian conjecture with degrees at most 150, two shapes have starting corner (7,42) and final corner (13/7,6): the standard (3,2)-pairs of degrees (147,98) and the standard (2,3)-pairs of degrees (98,147). We show that no such pair exists, the pair being normalised as in Corollary 5.21 of Guccione-Guccione-Valqui; no assumption is made on the polynomial attached to the starting corner, of which an arithmetic argument on regular corners shows that it has a single root. The two sides of the Newton polygon are described by the results of Guccione-Guccione-Valqui, and in suitable polynomial coordinates the pair is confined to an explicit finite system of polynomial equations. Its leading part is a pair of polynomials of degrees 18 and 12 in one variable with u3^2 - w2^3 of degree 7; up to the symmetries of the system there are exactly six such pairs, conjugate over a number field of degree 6. Over that field the remaining equations are solved by three steps of linear algebra, and the 46 compatibility conditions, polynomials in six unknowns, generate the unit ideal. The computation is exact and is reproduced by an ancillary script (SymPy, python-flint, PARI, and Singular for the Groebner bases). All statements are proved relative to the cited results. Nothing in this note has been checked by a third party.

papers.title: Unconditional irreducibility of characteristic polynomials of symmetric Rademacher matrices
papers.abstract: We prove that the characteristic polynomial of an $n\times n$ symmetric Rademacher matrix is irreducible over $\mathbb Q$ with probability $1-O(\exp(-c n^{1/4}))$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. The proof combines the zero-free half-plane for Dedekind zeta functions of Cureton and Thorner with the finite-field rank distribution theorem of Ferber, Jain, Sah, and Sawhney.

papers.title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
papers.abstract: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $\Delta_\xi$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.

papers.title: Upper bounds for nearly equal largest prime factors of consecutive integers
papers.abstract: Let \(p<q\) be the largest prime factors of \(n\) and \(n+1\), in either order. For \(X^{3/4+\eta}\le H\le X\), the number of \(n\in(X,X+H]\) with \(q/p\le1+d\) is \(O_\eta(dH\log(2+d\sqrt X)/(\log X)^2)\), uniformly for \(0<d\le1\). Imposing \(|n/(pq)-1|\le w\le1/2\) gives \(O_\eta(wdH/(\log X)^2)\). For fixed window widths both estimates hold down to \(H=X^{2/3+\eta}\). At \(H=X\), matching lower bounds give the order of the first count whenever \(d\sqrt X\ge(\log X)^{1+\delta}\) for fixed \(\delta>0\).

papers.title: Xia's equations for the Higman–McLaughlin (1961) conjecture: exact solution counts when the norm equation is replaced by its sum
papers.abstract: Every known finite flag-transitive projective plane is Desarguesian, and it is an old conjecture, first mentioned by Higman and McLaughlin in 1961, that there are no others. By theorems of Kantor and of Thas and Zagier, a counterexample of order $n$ would force $p=n^2+n+1$ to be prime and make the subgroup of order $n+1$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ a planar difference set. Then $n\equiv8\pmod{24}$, and from the difference set Xia derived a further necessary condition: a system of polynomial equations over a field of characteristic $3$ has a solution. The system consists of a Frobenius relation, a norm equation, an autocorrelation equation and a doubling equation, and Xia conjectured that it has no solution for $n>8$. We completely solve the norm-free system, obtained by replacing the norm equation by its sum over all indices: for every $n\equiv8\pmod{24}$ and every even divisor $\sigma$ of $n$ (the shift in the Frobenius relation), the resulting system has exactly $4\prod_i(3^{L_i}-1)$ solutions, where the $L_i$ are the lengths of explicit Frobenius orbits on roots of unity. So any proof of Xia's conjecture must use the norm equation itself. For $\sigma=2$ we show that, once the Fourier transform of the unknowns is fixed on the $(n/2)$-th roots of unity, the norm equation becomes two conditions, each involving only one eigenspace of an involution of the remaining parameters. For $n=2^e$ with $e\ge5$ odd the two conditions are not independent: the remaining parameters lie on a conic. Xia's system with $\sigma=2$ has at most $16\,(4/3)^{b}\,3^{n/8}$ solutions ($b\ge0$ is an explicit integer, $b=0$ when $16\mid n$), and at most $16(3^{n/8}-1)$ when $n=2^e$ with $e\ge5$ odd. For $8\mid n$, the analogous exact count, $4\prod_i(r^{L_i}-1)$, holds for the norm-free versions of Xia's systems in every characteristic $r$ with $r\nmid pn$ and $r\not\equiv-1$ modulo the $2$-part of $n$. Both conjectures remain open. Every result that this paper proves has also been proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, where Proposition 6.1 assumes Xia's Proposition 1.2.
